questions.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Fundamental Rights?
options: Fundamental Rights can be enforced by Law.
Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
The Fundamental Rights are mentioned in constitution from article 12 to 35.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution..

Key Points

• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Article 12 to 35.

• These rights are essential for the overall development of individuals and the preservation of human dignity.

• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced through the courts of law in India.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Rights

• Fundamental Rights are the basic human rights guaranteed to all individuals by the Constitution of India. These rights are crucial for the protection and development of individuals.

• They are meant to promote the ideal of political democracy and prevent the arbitrary use of power by the state.

• Some of the key Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).

• These rights are enforceable by the courts, and individuals can approach the judiciary to seek protection and enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.

• Enforcement of Fundamental Rights

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts to enforce these rights if they are violated.

• The Supreme Court and High Courts have the power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

• Writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari are used to enforce these rights.

• Right to Life (Article 21)

• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.

• This article ensures that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.

• The Right to Life under Article 21 has been interpreted by the Supreme Court to include various rights such as the right to live with human dignity, right to livelihood, right to health, right to education, and more.

questions.q: Under which scheme are collateral free loans of up to ₹10 Lakh extended by the Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana.

Key Points

• Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched by the government of India to provide loans up to ₹10 Lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

• These loans are classified as MUDRA loans under PMMY and are given by commercial banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.

• The scheme was launched on 8 April 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency Limited, which provides funding support to the micro-enterprise sector.

Additional Information

• National Strategy for Financial Inclusion

• It is a strategy prepared by the Reserve Bank of India to provide access to formal financial services in an affordable manner.

• The strategy aims at promoting financial education, financial literacy, and consumer protection.

• It includes various stakeholders like banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), micro-finance institutions (MFIs), and insurance companies.

• It emphasizes the need for a robust digital financial ecosystem to achieve universal financial access.

• Stand Up India scheme

• It was launched on 5 April 2016 by the Government of India.

• The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and women by providing loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore.

• It ensures that each bank branch provides at least one loan to SC/ST and one to women borrowers.

• Stand Up India scheme provides handholding support and guidance to borrowers during the loan tenure.

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana

• Launched on 28 August 2014, it aims to provide universal access to banking facilities with at least one basic banking account for every household.

• The scheme promotes financial inclusion by ensuring access to financial services such as bank savings and deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.

• It allows direct benefit transfer (DBT) to accounts opened under PMJDY, ensuring transparency and reducing leakages.

• The scheme also provides an overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000 to account holders.

questions.q: Which of the following festivals observed in Assam is majorly celebrated by Vaishnavites?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Doljatra.

Key Points

• Doljatra, also known as Dol Purnima or Dol Yatra, is a major festival celebrated by the Vaishnavites of Assam.

• It is observed on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna (February-March).

• Doljatra marks the arrival of spring and is a festival of colors, similar to Holi.

• During this festival, people worship Lord Krishna and celebrate his divine play (Leela) with Radha and the Gopis.

Additional Information

• Bihu

• Bihu is the most important festival of Assam, celebrated thrice a year as Rongali Bihu, Kongali Bihu, and Bhogali Bihu.

• It is primarily an agricultural festival associated with the changing seasons.

• Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April to mark the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.

• Kongali Bihu is observed in October and is a solemn occasion with less merrymaking.

• Bhogali Bihu, celebrated in January, marks the end of the harvest season and is characterized by feasts and bonfires.

• Ambuchi Mela

• Ambuchi Mela is a significant festival held at the Kamakhya Temple in Assam.

• It is celebrated during the monsoon season in June and marks the annual menstruation of the goddess Kamakhya.

• Devotees from all over the country visit the temple to seek blessings during this time.

• The temple remains closed for three days, and on the fourth day, the doors are opened with great festivities.

• Rongker

• Rongker is a traditional festival of the Karbi tribe in Assam.

• It is celebrated to appease local deities and ensure a bountiful harvest.

• The festival involves elaborate rituals, prayers, and sacrifices to seek the blessings of the gods.

• Rongker is usually observed in the month of April or May.

questions.q: Which of the following group of months is the coldest in North India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is December and January.

Key Points

• December and January are the peak winter months in North India.

• During these months, temperatures can drop significantly, often reaching sub-zero levels in hilly areas.

• These months typically experience the lowest average temperatures compared to other months.

• Cold waves and frost are common during December and January, making it the coldest period in the region.

Additional Information

• Winter Season in North India

• The winter season in North India typically starts in late November and lasts until February.

• December and January are considered the coldest months due to the high pressure areas that develop over the region, leading to cold waves.

• Temperature variations are significant, with some plains experiencing night temperatures close to freezing, while day temperatures remain relatively moderate.

• Snowfall is common in the Himalayan regions, attracting tourists to hill stations like Shimla, Manali, and Gulmarg.

• Climate Influences

• The climate of North India is influenced by the Himalayas and the Thar Desert. The Himalayas act as a barrier to the cold winds from Central Asia, while the Thar Desert brings dry and cold air.

• Western disturbances, which are weather phenomena originating from the Mediterranean region, also bring cold air and precipitation to North India during the winter months.

• Impact on Daily Life

• The cold weather affects daily life, especially for those who do not have adequate heating facilities. It can lead to health issues such as hypothermia and respiratory problems.

• Agricultural activities are also impacted as frost can damage crops, leading to economic losses for farmers.

questions.q: Some of the talas invented by _ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is M. Balamuralikrishna.

Key Points

• M. Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic vocalist, musician, multi-instrumentalist, playback singer, composer, and character actor.

• He was known for his deep knowledge of both the theoretical and practical aspects of Carnatic music.

• He invented new ragas as well as talas, including the ones mentioned: Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, and Navamukhi.

• His contributions to Carnatic music earned him several prestigious awards, including the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Additional Information

• Carnatic Music

• Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with the southern part of the Indian subcontinent, with its foundations in ancient Hindu traditions.

• It is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music that evolved from ancient Hindu traditions, the other subgenre being Hindustani music.

• The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on vocal music; most compositions are written to be sung, and even when played on instruments, they are meant to be performed in a singing style (known as gayaki).

• Tala

• Tala, literally meaning "clap," is the term used in Indian classical music to refer to musical meter, that is, any rhythmic beat or strike that measures musical time.

• It is a series of beats that are cyclically repeated.

• Talas can have different numbers of beats, and the cycle of beats is divided into sections called "angas," which can be of varying lengths.

• Instruments Played by M. Balamuralikrishna

• Besides being a renowned vocalist, M. Balamuralikrishna was proficient in playing the violin, viola, mridangam, and kanjira.

• His multifaceted talent in playing various instruments added to his versatility and depth as a musician.

questions.q: In which year was the temple entry movement started by Bhimrao Ambedkar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1927.

Key Points

• The temple entry movement was started by Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar in the year 1927.

• This movement was aimed at allowing untouchables or Dalits to enter Hindu temples.

• Dr. Ambedkar led several Dalits to enter the Kalaram Temple in Nashik, Maharashtra, which was significant for its religious importance.

• The movement was part of a broader effort by Dr. Ambedkar to fight against the caste system and for the rights of Dalits.

Additional Information

• Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was an Indian jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer who inspired the Dalit Buddhist movement and campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits).

• He was the principal architect of the Constitution of India and served as the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India.

• Ambedkar’s efforts to eradicate social evils like untouchability and caste restrictions were profound and were recognized by the nation, which posthumously awarded him the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian award.

• Temple Entry Movement

• The Temple Entry Movement was part of the broader Dalit movement in India aimed at securing equal rights for untouchables.

• It was a social movement aimed at ensuring that Dalits had the right to enter temples and participate in religious activities, which were traditionally denied to them due to caste-based discrimination.

• The movement was significant in highlighting the issues faced by Dalits and in pushing for social reforms.

• Kalaram Temple Satyagraha

• The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha was a landmark protest led by Dr. Ambedkar in 1930, where he and his followers attempted to enter the Kalaram Temple in Nashik.

• The protest was aimed at challenging the traditional prohibitions that barred Dalits from entering temples.

• Though the attempt faced significant resistance, it marked a crucial step in the fight against caste-based discrimination and temple entry restrictions.

• Impact of the Movement

• The Temple Entry Movement significantly contributed to the social reforms in India, paving the way for the eventual abolition of untouchability.

• It also helped in raising awareness about the plight of Dalits and inspired future generations to continue the fight for equality and justice.

• The movement laid the groundwork for legal and social changes, including the enactment of laws that prohibited untouchability and discrimination.

questions.q: Who among the following dancers was the first one from the state of Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan Award?
questions.solution:

Key Points

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was an iconic Indian classical dancer, known for his contributions to the Odissi dance form.

• He was the first dancer from Odisha to be conferred with the Padma Vibhushan Award in 2000, which is the second-highest civilian award in India.

• Kelucharan Mohapatra played a pivotal role in popularizing Odissi dance both in India and internationally.

• His dedication and contributions to the field of dance have earned him numerous accolades and recognition, making him a revered figure in Indian classical dance.

Additional Information

• Padma Awards

• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in 1954. They are awarded in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

• Padma Vibhushan: It is the second-highest civilian award in India, given for exceptional and distinguished service.

• Padma Bhushan: It is the third-highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished service of a high order.

• Padma Shri: It is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished service in any field.

• Odissi Dance

• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.

• It is known for its fluid movements, intricate gestures, and expressive facial expressions, often depicting mythological stories and devotional themes.

• Odissi dance has a rich history, dating back to ancient times and is closely associated with the temples of Odisha.

• Kelucharan Mohapatra is renowned for reviving and popularizing this ancient dance form, making significant contributions to its development and preservation.

• He achieved the title of International Master (IM) in chess.

• Gupta has participated in several national and international chess tournaments, showcasing his strategic skills.

• He is known for his analytical prowess and has contributed to the growth of chess in India.

Additional Information

• Chess Terminologies and Titles:

• International Master (IM): This is a high-level title awarded by the World Chess Federation (FIDE). It is one step below the Grandmaster (GM) title.

• Grandmaster (GM): The highest title awarded in chess, signifying a player of exceptional skill and achievement.

• FIDE: Fédération Internationale des Échecs or International Chess Federation, the governing body of international chess competition.

• Chess Rating: A system used by FIDE to estimate the strength of players, based on their performance in tournaments.

• India has produced several notable chess players including Viswanathan Anand, the former World Chess Champion.

• Chess Strategies:

• Opening: The initial phase of the game where players develop their pieces and control the center of the board.

• Middle Game: The phase where players engage in tactical maneuvers and strategic planning.

• Endgame: The final phase where the number of pieces is reduced, and players aim to checkmate the opponent’s king.

• Importance of Chess:

• Chess improves cognitive skills such as memory, problem-solving, and critical thinking.

• It enhances concentration and patience among players.

• Playing chess promotes strategic and analytical thinking, beneficial for various aspects of life.

questions.q: Which ocean is encircling the continent of Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude?

questions.q: Which types of gametes are found in Spirogyra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Isogamous and non-flagellated.

Key Points

• Spirogyra is a genus of filamentous green algae that is commonly found in fresh water.

• The gametes in Spirogyra are isogamous, meaning they are morphologically similar or identical.

• Isogamous gametes in Spirogyra are non-flagellated, meaning they do not have flagella and thus do not have the ability to move independently.

• During reproduction, Spirogyra undergoes a process called conjugation, where gametes from different filaments join together to form a zygote.

Additional Information

• Isogamy:

• Isogamy refers to a type of sexual reproduction involving gametes of similar morphology (shape and size), differing only in their allelic composition.

• In isogamous species, the gametes are often referred to as "+" and "-" types rather than male and female.

• Flagella:

• Flagella are long, whip-like appendages that protrude from the cell body and enable many protozoa, bacteria, and spermatozoa to swim.

• Non-flagellated gametes lack these appendages and thus rely on other means for movement, such as water currents.

• Conjugation in Spirogyra:

• Conjugation in Spirogyra is a form of sexual reproduction where two filaments align side by side and form conjugation tubes.

• Protoplasts from one filament move through these tubes and fuse with the protoplasts of the other filament to form zygospores.

• Zygospores are thick-walled and can survive harsh conditions. Upon germination, they undergo meiosis to produce new haploid filaments.

• Spirogyra:

• Spirogyra is known for its spiral arrangement of chloroplasts, which is unique and easily identifiable.

• It is commonly referred to as "pond scum" and can form dense mats on the surface of freshwater bodies.

• Spirogyra plays an important role in the ecosystem by producing oxygen through photosynthesis and serving as food for aquatic organisms.

questions.q: The radii of two circles are 8 cm and 15 cm. The perimeter of the circle having area equal to the sum of the areas of the two circles (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If the area of a circle is equal to the sum of the areas of two circles with radii r₁ and r₂, then the new radius R satisfies R² = r₁² + r₂².

The given radii 8 cm and 15 cm form a Pythagorean triplet with 17 cm.

Thus, the radius of the new circle is R = 17 cm.

Perimeter = 2πR = 2 × π × 17 = 34π cm.

∴ The correct answer is 34π cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the first circle (r₁) = 8 cm

Radius of the second circle (r₂) = 15 cm



Formula Used:

Area of a circle = πr²

Perimeter of a circle = 2πr

Calculations:

⇒ Area of first circle = π × 8² = 64π cm²

⇒ Area of second circle = π × 15² = 225π cm²

⇒ Total Area = 64π + 225π = 289π cm²

⇒ Let the radius of the new circle be R.

⇒ Area of the new circle = πR² = 289π

⇒ R² = 289

⇒ R = √289 = 17 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the new circle = 2 × π × R

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × π × 17 = 34π cm

∴ The correct answer is 34π cm.

Additional Information

Perimeter and Area of a Circle

The perimeter (circumference) of a circle is 2πr, and its area is πr², where r is the radius of the circle.

Area Proportionality Concept

When the area of a circle equals the sum of the areas of two other circles, their radii naturally form a Pythagorean triplet satisfying the equation R² = r₁² + r₂².

Circumference Proportionality Concept

If the circumference of a given circle equals the sum of the circumferences of two other circles, then the new radius directly satisfies R = r₁ + r₂.

Semi-Circle Formulas

The area of a semi-circle is πr² ÷ 2, and its total perimeter including the base diameter is πr + 2r.

10 Years Ago Ratio = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 parts)

Multiply present ratio by 3 and past ratio by 2 to equate differences → Present = 9 : 3, Past = 8 : 2

Change in ratio = 9 − 8 = 1 part = 10 years.

Present age difference = 9 − 3 = 6 parts = 6 × 10 = 60 years.

∴ The correct answer is 60 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Current age of Ghanshyam is thrice the current age of Akash.

10 years ago, Ghanshyam was 4 times as old as Akash.



Calculations:

Let the current age of Akash be x years.

⇒ Current age of Ghanshyam = 3x years

Age of Akash 10 years ago = (x − 10) years

Age of Ghanshyam 10 years ago = (3x − 10) years

According to the given condition, 10 years ago Ghanshyam was 4 times as old as Akash:

⇒ 3x − 10 = 4 × (x − 10)

⇒ 3x − 10 = 4x − 40

⇒ x = 40 − 10

⇒ x = 30

⇒ Current age of Akash = 30 years

⇒ Current age of Ghanshyam = 3 × 30 = 90 years

⇒ Difference in their current ages = 90 − 30 = 60 years

∴ The correct answer is 60 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The absolute difference between the ages of two individuals always remains constant at any point in time. This fundamental property is heavily used to equate ratio differences in age-related problems.

Ratio & Proportion Basics

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b, their actual values can be assumed to be ax and bx, where x is a common multiplier representing the value of one proportional unit.

Linear Equations in Ages

Most age-related word problems can be converted into standard linear equations of the form ax + b = cy + d, which can be rapidly solved by simplifying the variables on one side.

Since cotA is the reciprocal of tanA, the equation tanA + 1/tanA = 2 implies tanA = 1.

This means cotA = 1/1 = 1.

Substitute these values directly: tan² A + cot² A = 1² + 1² = 2.

⇒ (tanA + cotA)² = 2²

⇒ tan² A + cot² A + 2 × tanA × cotA = 4

⇒ tan² A + cot² A + 2 × 1 = 4

⇒ tan² A + cot² A = 4 − 2

⇒ tan² A + cot² A = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Higher Powers Identity

If x + 1/x = 2, then for any positive integer n, the value of xⁿ + 1/xⁿ will always be equal to 2.

Squaring Concept for Variables

If x + 1/x = k, then the sum of their squares is derived directly as x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Basic Trigonometric Conversions

questions.q: An article is sold for ₹747 after successive discounts of 17% and x%. If the marked price of the article is ₹1,600, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Price after 1st discount of 17% = 1600 × (100 − 17)% = 1600 × 83% = ₹1328

Selling Price after 2nd discount (x%) = ₹747

Amount of 2nd discount = 1328 − 747 = ₹581

Value of x = (581 ÷ 1328) × 100 = 43.75

∴ The correct answer is 43.75.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,600

Selling Price (SP) = ₹747

First discount (D₁) = 17%

Second discount (D₂) = x%



Formula Used:

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

Calculation:

⇒ 747 = 1600 × (1 − 17/100) × (1 − x/100)

⇒ 747 = 1600 × (83/100) × (1 − x/100)

⇒ 747 = 1328 × (1 − x/100)

⇒ 1 − x/100 = 747 ÷ 1328

⇒ 1 − x/100 = 9/16

⇒ x/100 = 1 − 9/16

⇒ x/100 = 7/16

⇒ x = (7 × 100) ÷ 16

⇒ x = 700 ÷ 16 = 43.75

∴ The correct answer is 43.75.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the article. SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts of x% and y% are given successively, the equivalent single discount percentage is [x + y − (x × y)/100]%.

Profit/Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.q: Two goods trains 132 m and 108 m in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks. The first train is running at a speed of 32 km/h and the second at a speed of 40 km/h. How much time will they take to cross each other after meeting?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance = 132 + 108 = 240 m

Relative speed (opposite directions) = 32 + 40 = 72 km/h

Convert speed to m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 s

∴ The correct answer is 12 s.

Alternate Method



Given:

Length of first train (L₁) = 132 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 108 m

Speed of first train (V₁) = 32 km/h

Speed of second train (V₂) = 40 km/h

Formula Used:

Time taken to cross = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

For trains moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = V₁ + V₂

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 132 + 108 = 240 m

⇒ Relative Speed = V₁ + V₂ = 32 + 40 = 72 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 s

∴ The correct answer is 12 s.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = |V₁ − V₂|.

Crossing a Stationary Object with Length

When a train crosses a bridge, tunnel, or platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the train's length and the object's length: Total Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ + Lₒbjₑ꜀ₜ.

Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train: Total Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ.

Speed Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by (5/18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18/5).

questions.q: On dividing a number by 55, we get 28 as the remainder. On dividing the same number by 11, what is the remainder?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a number is divided by D₁ leaving remainder R, and we divide it by D₂ (where D₁ is exactly divisible by D₂):

New Remainder = Remainder of (R ÷ D₂)

Here, D₁ (55) is exactly divisible by D₂ (11).

So, divide the first remainder 28 by 11 directly.

28 ÷ 11 = 2 with a remainder of 6.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

A number when divided by 55 leaves a remainder of 28.

Formula Used:

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder



Calculations:

⇒ Let the quotient be k and the number be N.

⇒ N = 55 × k + 28

⇒ We need to find the remainder when N is divided by 11.

⇒ Let us express N in terms of multiples of 11.

⇒ N = (11 × 5 × k) + (11 × 2 + 6)

⇒ N = 11 × (5k + 2) + 6

⇒ Since 11 × (5k + 2) is completely divisible by 11, the remaining value 6 is the remainder.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Division Algorithm

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. This equation forms the basis of all basic remainder theorem problems.

Divisibility Condition

This direct remainder shortcut only works when the first divisor (55) is an exact multiple of the second divisor (11). If it is not, the answer cannot be determined.

Negative Remainder Concept

For easier calculations in complex problems, remainders can also be treated as negative. For example, 28 ÷ 11 gives remainder 6, which is equivalent to a negative remainder of −5 (since 11 − 5 = 6).

questions.q: Vipul spends 30% of his monthly income on rent, 60% of the remaining on groceries, and 40% of the remaining on others. If he saves ₹ 7056 in a month, then how much (in ₹) does he spend on groceries?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Savings % = 100% × (100% − 30%) × (100% − 60%) × (100% − 40%)

⇒ Savings = 100% × 0.7 × 0.4 × 0.6 = 16.8%

Given 16.8% of Income = ₹ 7056 ⇒ 1% = 7056 ÷ 16.8 = ₹ 420

Grocery % = 60% of the first remaining (70%) = 42%

Amount spent on groceries = 42% × 420 = ₹ 17640

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 17640.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rent spend = 30% of Income

Grocery spend = 60% of remaining

Other spend = 40% of remaining

Savings = ₹ 7056

Formula Used:

Remaining Amount = Initial Amount × (100 − Spend %)/100



Calculations:

⇒ Let the total monthly income be x.

⇒ Amount left after paying rent = x − 0.30x = 0.70x

⇒ Amount spent on groceries = 60% of 0.70x = 0.42x

⇒ Amount left after grocery spend = 0.70x − 0.42x = 0.28x

⇒ Amount spent on others = 40% of 0.28x = 0.112x

⇒ Final Savings = 0.28x − 0.112x = 0.168x

⇒ 0.168x = 7056

⇒ x = 7056 ÷ 0.168 = ₹ 42000

⇒ Amount spent on groceries = 0.42 × 42000 = ₹ 17640

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 17640.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Model

When a base value is continuously reduced by varying percentages, the final value is calculated as: Final = Base × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100)...

Multiplier Fraction Method

Instead of decimals, use fractions: 30% = 3/10 (remaining 7/10), 60% = 3/5 (remaining 2/5), 40% = 2/5 (remaining 3/5). Total remaining fraction = 7/10 × 2/5 × 3/5 = 42/250 = 16.8%.

Reverse Calculation

To find initial income from final savings directly, divide the savings successively by the remaining percentage factors: Base = Savings ÷ [ (1 − p₁) × (1 − p₂) ... ]

questions.q: A man buys 10 kg of wheat at a rate of ₹26/kg. The wheat is mixed with 6 kg of other good quality of wheat to get a mixture at a price of ₹35/kg. The price of good quality wheat per kg (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Alligation Method:

Quantity Ratio = 10 kg : 6 kg = 5 : 3

By alligation rule: (x − 35) ÷ (35 − 26) = 5 ÷ 3

⇒ (x − 35) ÷ 9 = 5 ÷ 3

⇒ x − 35 = 15 ⇒ x = 50

∴ The correct answer is ₹50.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity of regular wheat = 10 kg at ₹26/kg

Quantity of good quality wheat = 6 kg at ₹x/kg

Resulting mixture price = ₹35/kg

Formula Used:

Weighted Average Price = (Q₁ × P₁ + Q₂ × P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂)



Calculations:

⇒ Total quantity of the mixture = 10 + 6 = 16 kg

⇒ Total cost of 10 kg wheat = 10 × 26 = ₹260

⇒ Total cost of 6 kg good quality wheat = 6 × x = ₹6x

⇒ Total cost of 16 kg mixture = 16 × 35 = ₹560

⇒ 260 + 6x = 560

⇒ 6x = 560 − 260

⇒ 6x = 300

⇒ x = 50

∴ The correct answer is ₹50.

Additional Information

Alligation Rule

When two ingredients of different prices are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is given by: Quantity 1 : Quantity 2 = (Price 2 − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Price 1).

Weighted Average

The mean or average value of a mixture is calculated using the weighted average formula: Mean = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Replacement in Mixtures

When a quantity 'y' is replaced 'n' times from an initial mixture volume 'x', the remaining quantity of the pure substance is given by: x(1 − y ÷ x)ⁿ.

questions.q: What is the length (in cm) of each side of a cube if the volume of a cube is 13,824 cm3?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find the side of the cube, we need the cube root of the given volume (13824 cm³).

The unit digit of 13824 is 4, which means its cube root will also end in 4 (since 4³ ends in 4).

Ignoring the last three digits (824), the remaining number is 13.

The largest perfect cube less than or equal to 13 is 8 (which is 2³), so the tens digit is 2.

Thus, the side length is 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Volume of the cube = 13824 cm³

Formula Used:

Volume of a cube = a³ (where a is the side of the cube)



Calculations:

⇒ a³ = 13824

⇒ a³ = 2⁹ × 3³

⇒ a = (2⁹ × 3³)¹/³

⇒ a = 2³ × 3¹

⇒ a = 8 × 3

⇒ a = 24 cm

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube with side length 'a' is calculated using the formula 6a².

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

The surface area excluding the top and bottom faces is known as lateral surface area, given by 4a².

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the main diagonal connecting two completely opposite corners of the cube is a√3.

questions.q: Pipe A takes 54​ of the time required by pipe B to fill an empty tank individually. When an outlet pipe C is also opened simultaneously with pipes A and B, it takes 54​ more time to fill the empty tank than it takes when only pipe A and pipe B are opened together. If it takes 40 hours to fill the tank when all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, in what time (in hours) will pipe C empty the full tank, operating alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Time taken by pipes A + B + C together = 40 hours.

Since A + B + C takes 4/5 more time than A + B, Time(A + B + C) = (1 + 4/5) × Time(A + B) = 9/5 × Time(A + B).

Time taken by A + B = 40 × (5/9) = 200/9 hours.

Let Total Work = LCM(40, 200/9) = 200 units.

Efficiency of C = Efficiency(A + B) − Efficiency(A + B + C) = 9 − 5 = 4 units/hour.

Time taken by C alone = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 50 hours.

questions.q: If the mean proportional between p and q is 12, then the possible values of p and q, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The mean proportional between two numbers p and q is given by √(pq).

⇒ √(pq) = 12 ⇒ pq = 144

Checking the given options for a product equal to 144:

⇒ 24 × 6 = 144

∴ The correct answer is 24, 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

Mean proportional between p and q = 12

Formula Used:

If b is the mean proportional between a and c, then b² = a × c.



Calculations:

⇒ As 12 is the mean proportional, p, 12, and q are in continued proportion.

⇒ p : 12 :: 12 : q

⇒ p ÷ 12 = 12 ÷ q

⇒ p × q = 12 × 12

⇒ pq = 144

Now, let's substitute the values from the given options to find which pair gives a product of 144:

⇒ Option 1: 3 × 38 = 114

⇒ Option 2: 3 × 28 = 84

⇒ Option 3: 24 × 6 = 144

⇒ Option 4: 24 × 16 = 384

⇒ Only Option 3 satisfies the condition (24 × 6 = 144).

∴ The correct answer is 24, 6.

Additional Information

Third Proportional

If c is the third proportional to a and b, then a : b :: b : c, which gives the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If d is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, then a : b :: c : d, which gives the formula d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given by a² : b². The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is given by √a : √b.

questions.q: A person purchased a table and a sofa for ₹28,000. He sold the sofa at a profit of 10% and the table at a profit 15.25%. If his total profit was 13%, then the difference between the cost price of the sofa and the table (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Alligation Method directly on profit percentages to find the ratio of their Cost Prices (CP):

Ratio of CP of Sofa to Table = (Table Profit % − Overall Profit %) : (Overall Profit % − Sofa Profit %)

⇒ Ratio = (15.25 − 13) : (13 − 10) = 2.25 : 3 = 225 : 300 = 3 : 4

Total CP parts = 3 + 4 = 7 parts ⇒ 7 parts = ₹28,000

⇒ 1 part = ₹4,000

Difference in CP = 4 parts − 3 parts = 1 part = ₹4,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of Sofa and Table = ₹28,000

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Sofa = 10%

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Table = 15.25%

⇒ Overall profit percentage on both = 13%

Formula Used:

We apply the Rule of Alligation to find the ratio of the Cost Prices of the two articles.



Calculations:

⇒ Let the CP of the Sofa be 3x and the CP of the Table be 4x.

⇒ Total CP = 3x + 4x = 7x

⇒ 7x = 28000

⇒ x = 28000 ÷ 7 = 4000

⇒ Required difference in CP = CP of Table − CP of Sofa

⇒ Difference = 4x − 3x = x

⇒ Difference = ₹4000

∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation in Profit & Loss

When two items are mixed or sold together at different profit/loss percentages, applying the alligation method yields the ratio of their Base Values, which is the Cost Price (CP) for profit and loss scenarios.

Weighted Average Formula

The overall profit percentage is the weighted average of the individual profit percentages. Formula: Overall % = (CP₁ × P₁ + CP₂ × P₂) ÷ (CP₁ + CP₂).

Handling Loss in Alligation

If an item is sold at a loss, its percentage must be written with a negative sign (e.g., −10%) in the alligation cross. The arithmetic difference must be carefully calculated considering the negative sign.

questions.q: If 3 tan A = 4 and A is an acute angle, then the value of 4sinA + 3cosA is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given 3 tan A = 4 ⇒ tan A = 4/3 = Perpendicular / Base.

The sides form a classic Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), so Hypotenuse = 5.

Therefore, sin A = 4/5 and cos A = 3/5.

Value of expression = 4 × (4/5) + 3 × (3/5) = 16/5 + 9/5 = 25/5 = 5.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method



Given:

⇒ 3 tan A = 4

⇒ tan A = 4/3

Formula Used:

⇒ tan A = P ÷ B (where P = Perpendicular, B = Base)

⇒ sin A = P ÷ H (where H = Hypotenuse)

⇒ cos A = B ÷ H

⇒ H = √(P² + B²)

Calculation:

⇒ From tan A = 4/3, let P = 4 and B = 3

⇒ H = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5

⇒ sin A = 4/5

⇒ cos A = 3/5

⇒ 4sin A + 3cos A = 4 × (4/5) + 3 × (3/5)

⇒ 4sin A + 3cos A = 16/5 + 9/5

⇒ 4sin A + 3cos A = 25/5 = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers a, b, and c that strictly satisfy a² + b² = c². Commonly tested triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Trigonometric Identities

The three core fundamental identities are sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

questions.q: A cell phone is available for Rs.600 or for Rs.300 cash down payment together with Rs.360 to be paid after two months. Find the rate of interest charged under this scheme.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Remaining Principal = Total Price − Down Payment = 600 − 300 = Rs. 300

Interest = Final Amount − Remaining Principal = 360 − 300 = Rs. 60

Time = 2 months = 2 ÷ 12 = 1/6 years

Rate (%) = (Interest × 100) ÷ (Principal × Time)

Rate = (60 × 100) ÷ (300 × 1/6) = 6000 ÷ 50 = 120%

∴ The correct answer is 120%.

Alternate Method



Given:

Cash price of the cell phone = Rs. 600

Down payment = Rs. 300

Amount paid after 2 months = Rs. 360

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, T = Time in years

Calculations:

⇒ Principal (P) = Cash price − Down payment

⇒ P = 600 − 300 = Rs. 300

⇒ Interest (I) = Amount paid − Principal

⇒ I = 360 − 300 = Rs. 60

⇒ Time (T) = 2 months = 2 ÷ 12 years = 1/6 years

⇒ 60 = (300 × R × (1/6)) ÷ 100

⇒ 60 = (300 ÷ 100) × R × (1/6)

⇒ 60 = 3 × R × (1/6)

⇒ 60 = R ÷ 2

⇒ R = 60 × 2 = 120%

∴ The correct answer is 120%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

In partial payment or down payment schemes, the interest is continually charged only on the unpaid balance (outstanding principal) for the specific time interval until the final settlement is made.

When the time is given in months rather than years, it must always be divided by 12 to convert it to annual terms before substituting it into the standard Simple Interest formula.

questions.q: For what value of K does the following system have an infinite number of solutions? x + 2Ky - 8 = 0 2x - y - 16 = 0
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For infinite solutions, the ratio of coefficients of x and y must be equal to the ratio of constants.

⇒ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂

⇒ 1/2 = 2K/(−1)

⇒ −2K = 1/2

⇒ K = −1/4

∴ The correct answer is −1/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: x + 2Ky − 8 = 0

Equation 2: 2x − y − 16 = 0

Formula Used:

For a system of linear equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to have an infinite number of solutions, the condition is:

a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

Calculation:

⇒ From the given equations, we identify the coefficients:

⇒ a₁ = 1, b₁ = 2K, c₁ = −8

⇒ a₂ = 2, b₂ = −1, c₂ = −16

⇒ Applying the condition for infinite solutions:

⇒ 1/2 = 2K/(−1) = −16−8​

⇒ 1/2 = −2K = 1/2

⇒ Equating the first two parts to find K:

⇒ 1/2 = −2K

⇒ K = −1/4

∴ The correct answer is −1/4.

Additional Information

Condition for Unique Solution

If a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the system has exactly one solution and the lines intersect at a single point.

Condition for No Solution

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the system has no solution and the lines are parallel.

Condition for Infinite Solutions

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the system has infinitely many solutions and the lines are coincident (overlapping).

questions.q: In △DEF , DE = 12 cm, EF = 15 cm, and ∠DEF = 90º. △DEF is congruent to △XYZ . If YZ = 15 cm, then what is the length of XZ?

Since △DEF ≅ △XYZ, their corresponding parts are equal. Therefore, XZ = DF.

In right-angled △DEF, DF is the hypotenuse as it is opposite to ∠DEF (90º).

Using the Pythagorean theorem: DF = √(DE² + EF²)

DF = √(12² + 15²) = √(144 + 225)

DF = √369 = √(9 × 41) = 3√41 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 3√41 cm.

Formula Used:

questions.q: Simplify the following expression. 133 ÷ 19 × 3 – 48 × 2 ÷ 24 + 841 ÷ { 45 – 16}

We will use the BODMAS/PEMDAS rule (Brackets, Orders (i.e., powers and square roots, etc.), Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction) to simplify the expression.

Calculation:

First, solve the expression inside the brackets { 45 – 16 }:

⇒ 45 – 16 = 29

Now simplify the expression step by step:

⇒ 133 ÷ 19 × 3 – 48 × 2 ÷ 24 + 841 ÷ 29

Perform the division and multiplication from left to right:

⇒ (133 ÷ 19) × 3 – (48 × 2) ÷ 24 + (841 ÷ 29)

⇒ 7 × 3 – 96 ÷ 24 + 29

⇒ 21 – 4 + 29

Perform the addition and subtraction from left to right:

⇒ 21 – 4 = 17

⇒ 17 + 29 = 46

The correct answer is option 1.
